analyticalDashboards.description: Dashboard for analyzing customer segmentation and lifetime value through loyalty activity, events, feedback, and NPS trends over time. It brings together key time-series views such as points earned/redeemed, reward and order value, event volume/value, feedback volume/sentiment, and response counts, plus a lifetime order count headline. By default it is filtered to the last 12 months, with optional store region and product filtering available.

By default it is filtered to the last 12 months and includes fiscal period/year filters that can be adjusted to focus the analysis.

memoryItems.description: GlobalMart metric conventions › Choosing a date dimension (compiled from docs/knowledge/metric-hierarchy.md)
memoryItems.instruction: GlobalMart has two date dimensions, and choosing the wrong one silently changes the answer.

memoryItems.description: GlobalMart metric conventions › Choosing a date dimension (compiled from docs/knowledge/metric-hierarchy.md)
memoryItems.instruction: Use `transaction_date` for operational questions: daily sales, footfall, stock movement. It is when the transaction happened.
memoryItems.title: Choosing a date dimension

memoryItems.description: GlobalMart metric conventions › Choosing a date dimension (compiled from docs/knowledge/metric-hierarchy.md)
memoryItems.instruction: Use `fiscal_date` for anything compared against a budget or reported by period, because the fiscal year does not start in January.
memoryItems.title: Choosing a date dimension

memoryItems.description: GlobalMart metric conventions › Choosing a date dimension (compiled from docs/knowledge/metric-hierarchy.md)
memoryItems.instruction: When a question says "last quarter" in a financial context it means a fiscal quarter, so group by `fiscal_date`.
memoryItems.title: Choosing a date dimension

memoryItems.description: GlobalMart metric conventions › Choosing a revenue metric (compiled from docs/knowledge/metric-hierarchy.md)
memoryItems.instruction: Three metrics have "revenue" in the name and they are not interchangeable.
memoryItems.title: Choosing a revenue metric

memoryItems.description: GlobalMart metric conventions › Choosing a revenue metric (compiled from docs/knowledge/metric-hierarchy.md)
memoryItems.instruction: Use `metric_l1_total_net_revenue` by default. Net revenue is after returns and discounts.
memoryItems.title: Choosing a revenue metric

memoryItems.description: GlobalMart metric conventions › Choosing a revenue metric (compiled from docs/knowledge/metric-hierarchy.md)
memoryItems.instruction: `metric_l1_sql_margin_bridge_gross_revenue` is gross, before returns and discounts. It exists for the margin bridge and is the wrong figure elsewhere.
memoryItems.title: Choosing a revenue metric

memoryItems.description: GlobalMart metric conventions › Choosing a revenue metric (compiled from docs/knowledge/metric-hierarchy.md)
memoryItems.instruction: `metric_l1_sql_net_sales_summary_net_revenue` agrees with total net revenue but is scoped to its own SQL dataset's grain, so it does not slice by every dimension.
memoryItems.title: Choosing a revenue metric

memoryItems.description: GlobalMart metric conventions › Metric layers (compiled from docs/knowledge/metric-hierarchy.md)
memoryItems.instruction: GlobalMart's metrics are layered, and the layer is in both the metric id and its tags, L1 through L5.
memoryItems.title: Metric layers

memoryItems.description: GlobalMart metric conventions › Metric layers (compiled from docs/knowledge/metric-hierarchy.md)
memoryItems.instruction: L1 metrics (`metric_l1_*`) are base aggregations over a single fact column. They are the only layer that touches a fact directly.
memoryItems.title: Metric layers

memoryItems.description: GlobalMart metric conventions › Metric layers (compiled from docs/knowledge/metric-hierarchy.md)
memoryItems.instruction: L2 metrics (`metric_l2_cross_*`) are ratios between two L1 metrics, such as order count over net revenue.
memoryItems.title: Metric layers

memoryItems.description: GlobalMart metric conventions › Metric layers (compiled from docs/knowledge/metric-hierarchy.md)
memoryItems.instruction: L3 metrics (`metric_l3_*`) apply a filter to an L1 or L2 metric, usually a WHERE on a dimension attribute such as channel type.
memoryItems.title: Metric layers

memoryItems.description: GlobalMart metric conventions › Metric layers (compiled from docs/knowledge/metric-hierarchy.md)
memoryItems.instruction: L4 and L5 metrics compose further on top of the lower layers.
memoryItems.title: Metric layers

memoryItems.description: GlobalMart metric conventions › Metric layers (compiled from docs/knowledge/metric-hierarchy.md)
memoryItems.instruction: Prefer the lowest layer that answers the question. Total net revenue is an L1 metric; net revenue for one channel is an existing L3 metric, not an L1 metric with a filter added.
memoryItems.title: Metric layers

metrics.description: Average NPS score across NPS Response records in the current filter context, calculated directly from the underlying NPS score fact.
metrics.title: Average Total NPS Score

metrics.description: Tracks the total number of customer events by summing the Event Count from the Customer Event dataset. Use it to monitor overall event volume and compare activity across time periods, segments, or other breakdowns.
metrics.title: Total Event Count (Customer Event)

metrics.description: Sums the Event Value from the Customer Event dataset to show the total value generated by customer events. Use it to track overall event value over time or by different segments and breakdowns in reports and dashboards.
metrics.title: Total Event Value (Customer Event)

metrics.description: Total number of customer feedback items, calculated by summing the Feedback Count values in the Customer Feedback dataset. Use this metric to monitor overall feedback volume and analyze trends by time, product, region, or other available breakdowns.
metrics.title: Total Feedback Count (Customer Feedback)

metrics.description: Shows the overall sentiment captured in customer feedback by summing the Sentiment Score across feedback records. Use it to compare total feedback tone across segments or time periods based on the filters applied.
metrics.title: Total Sentiment Score (Customer Feedback)

metrics.description: Shows the total monetary value of orders that are associated with earned loyalty points by summing Order Amount from the Loyalty Points Earned dataset. Use it to track overall order value/volume in loyalty-focused analyses and reporting.
metrics.title: Total Order Amount (Loyalty Points Earned)

metrics.description: Sums the Points values to show the total number of loyalty points earned. Use it to track overall points accrual and compare earned points across relevant slices such as time, customer segments, or other available breakdowns.
metrics.title: Total Points (Loyalty Points Earned)

metrics.description: Sums all loyalty points redeemed across transactions to show overall redemption volume. Use it to monitor redemption trends over time or break down redeemed points by customer, program, or other available dimensions.
metrics.title: Total Points Redeemed (Loyalty Points Redeemed)

metrics.description: Shows the total monetary value of rewards customers have redeemed by summing Reward Value from the Loyalty Points Redeemed data. Use it to monitor overall redemption value over time or compare redemption value across customer segments.
metrics.title: Total Reward Value (Loyalty Points Redeemed)

metrics.description: Totals the NPS Score values from NPS Response records for the current filter context (such as a time period or segment). Use it to understand the overall volume of NPS scoring across the selected responses and to compare totals across slices of the data.
metrics.title: Total NPS Score (NPS Response)

metrics.description: Shows the total number of NPS survey responses by summing the Response Count from the NPS Response data. Use it to track overall response volume and to provide context when interpreting other NPS metrics.
metrics.title: Total Response Count (NPS Response)

metrics.description: Tracks the total number of tier change events by summing the Change Count from the Tier Change dataset. Use it to monitor overall tier change volume for the selected time period or business segment.
metrics.title: Total Change Count (Tier Change)

metrics.description: Shows the total of Average Order Value from the Customer Lifetime Value dataset across the currently selected customers and any applied filters. Use it to monitor how typical order size contributes to overall customer lifetime value in reporting.
metrics.title: Total Average Order Value (Customer Lifetime Value)

metrics.description: Total number of orders accumulated over a customer’s lifetime, based on the Customer Lifetime Value snapshot. Use this metric to understand overall customer purchase frequency and compare lifetime ordering behavior across segments.
metrics.title: Total Lifetime Order Count (Customer Lifetime Value)

metrics.description: Shows the total revenue generated across customers over their lifetime by summing the Lifetime Revenue measure from the Customer Lifetime Value dataset. Use it to quantify overall customer lifetime value revenue for the current selection (such as a customer segment or time filter).
metrics.title: Total Lifetime Revenue (Customer Lifetime Value)

metrics.description: Sums customers’ Frequency Quartile (Recency, Frequency, Monetary (RFM)) values from the Customer RFM Segments dataset to produce a total frequency-quartile score for the currently selected customer set. Use it to quantify and compare overall purchase-frequency quartile levels across segments or filters in Recency, Frequency, Monetary (RFM) analysis.
metrics.title: Total Frequency Quartile (RFM) (Customer RFM Segments)

metrics.description: Totals the Monetary Quartile (Recency, Frequency, Monetary (RFM)) scores from the Customer RFM Segments dataset, letting you see the overall monetary quartile value for customers within the current filters or grouping. Useful for comparing relative customer monetary contribution across segments.
metrics.title: Total Monetary Quartile (RFM) (Customer RFM Segments)

metrics.description: Adds up customers’ Recency Quartile (Recency, Frequency, Monetary (RFM)) scores from the Customer RFM Segments dataset to produce a single total recency-quartile value for the selected customers or segment.
metrics.title: Total Recency Quartile (RFM) (Customer RFM Segments)

metrics.description: Compares customer event activity to customer event value by calculating the difference between total event count and total event value. Use it to see whether changes in event volume are outpacing (or lagging) changes in the value generated, across time periods or business segments.
metrics.title: Event Count (Customer Event) vs Event Value (Customer Event) Change

metrics.description: Shows the net difference between total Customer Event Event Value and total Loyalty Points Earned for the same selection of data. Use it to quickly see whether event value is higher or lower than points earned when analyzing by time period, segment, or other breakdowns.
metrics.title: Event Value (Customer Event) vs Points (Loyalty Points Earned) Change

metrics.description: Calculates the difference between total loyalty points earned and the total order amount tied to those earned points. Use it to compare points accrual against the underlying order value and spot gaps between points issued and the purchase volume generating them.
metrics.title: Points (Loyalty Points Earned) vs Order Amount (Loyalty Points Earned) Change

metrics.description: Shows the net difference between the total order amount tied to loyalty points earned and the total reward value tied to loyalty points redeemed. Use it to see whether loyalty-driven purchasing value is outweighing redemption value when comparing across time periods or customer segments.
metrics.title: Order Amount (Loyalty Points Earned) vs Reward Value (Loyalty Points Redeemed) Change

metrics.description: Shows the difference between the total reward value from redeemed loyalty points and the total NPS score within the current filter context. Use it to compare how redemption value is changing relative to customer satisfaction scoring across the same time period or segments.
metrics.title: Reward Value (Loyalty Points Redeemed) vs NPS Score (NPS Response) Change

metrics.description: Calculates the difference between the total NPS Score and the total number of NPS survey responses in the current selection. Use it to compare overall NPS scoring volume against response volume and see whether score totals are keeping pace with response counts.
metrics.title: NPS Score (NPS Response) vs Response Count (NPS Response) Change

metrics.description: Measures the gap between NPS survey response volume and the total sentiment captured in customer feedback by subtracting Total Sentiment Score from Total Response Count. Use it to see whether changes in response volume are outpacing or lagging behind shifts in overall feedback sentiment for the same time period or filters.
metrics.title: Response Count (NPS Response) vs Sentiment Score (Customer Feedback) Change

metrics.description: Measures the net difference between total customer sentiment and total feedback volume by subtracting Total Feedback Count from Total Sentiment Score. Use it to see whether sentiment levels are high or low relative to how much feedback was received within the same filters or time period.
metrics.title: Sentiment Score (Customer Feedback) vs Feedback Count (Customer Feedback) Change

metrics.description: Net difference between the total number of customer feedback items and the total number of tier change events for the selected slice of data. Use it to see whether feedback volume is higher or lower than tier changes over a given time period or business segment.
metrics.title: Feedback Count (Customer Feedback) vs Change Count (Tier Change) Change

metrics.description: Shows the difference between the total number of tier change events and customers’ total lifetime order count. Use it to gauge whether tier changes are happening more or less frequently relative to overall customer purchase activity.
metrics.title: Change Count (Tier Change) vs Lifetime Order Count (Customer Lifetime Value) Change

metrics.description: Shows the difference between customers’ total lifetime order count and total lifetime revenue from the Customer Lifetime Value snapshot to highlight how purchase frequency compares to revenue. Use it to identify segments where order volume and revenue are moving out of sync.
metrics.title: Lifetime Order Count (Customer Lifetime Value) vs Lifetime Revenue (Customer Lifetime Value) Change

metrics.description: Calculates the difference between Total Lifetime Revenue and Total Average Order Value for the currently selected customers and any applied filters. Use it to quantify how overall customer lifetime value revenue compares with typical order size within the current reporting scope.
metrics.title: Lifetime Revenue (Customer Lifetime Value) vs Average Order Value (Customer Lifetime Value) Change

metrics.description: Shows the net difference between customers’ Average Order Value (from the Customer Lifetime Value snapshot) and their Recency Quartile score from Recency, Frequency, Monetary (RFM) segmentation (the process of dividing customers or data into groups by shared characteristics). Use it to compare order value against recency-based customer segments and see whether value trends higher or lower relative to recency ranking.
metrics.title: Average Order Value (Customer Lifetime Value) vs Recency Quartile (RFM) (Customer RFM Segments) Change

metrics.description: Shows the net difference between customers’ total Recency quartile score and total Frequency quartile score within the current filters or Recency, Frequency, Monetary (RFM) segment. Use it to gauge whether the selected customer group skews more toward recency (higher values) or frequency (lower values) overall.
metrics.title: Recency Quartile (RFM) (Customer RFM Segments) vs Frequency Quartile (RFM) (Customer RFM Segments) Change

metrics.description: Shows whether customers’ Recency, Frequency, Monetary (RFM) frequency quartile score is higher or lower than their Recency, Frequency, Monetary (RFM) monetary quartile score by calculating the difference between the two totals for the currently selected customer set. Use it in Recency, Frequency, Monetary (RFM) segmentation (the process of dividing customers or data into groups by shared characteristics) analysis to compare frequency-driven value versus spend-driven value across segments or filters.
metrics.title: Frequency Quartile (RFM) (Customer RFM Segments) vs Monetary Quartile (RFM) (Customer RFM Segments) Change

metrics.description: Totals customers’ Monetary Quartile (Recency, Frequency, Monetary (RFM)) scores, restricted to the North region. Use it to compare the overall monetary value segment score for North against other regions or when slicing analysis by other attributes.

sql.statement:
SELECT
    c.customer_id,
    c.customer_name,
    COUNT(DISTINCT oh.order_id) AS lifetime_order_count,
    SUM(ol.revenue) AS lifetime_revenue,
    AVG(ol.revenue) AS avg_order_value,
    MAX(oh.order_date) AS last_order_date,
    (EXTRACT(DAY FROM MAX(oh.order_date)) - EXTRACT(DAY FROM MIN(oh.order_date))) / 365.0 AS customer_age_years
FROM {{ datasource_schema }}.dim_customer c
LEFT JOIN {{ datasource_schema }}.fact_order_header oh ON c.customer_id = oh.customer_id
LEFT JOIN {{ datasource_schema }}.fact_order_line ol ON oh.order_id = ol.order_id
GROUP BY 1, 2

sql.statement:
SELECT
    c.customer_id,
    NTILE(4) OVER (ORDER BY MAX(oh.order_date)) AS recency_quartile,
    NTILE(4) OVER (ORDER BY COUNT(DISTINCT oh.order_id)) AS frequency_quartile,
    NTILE(4) OVER (ORDER BY SUM(ol.revenue)) AS monetary_quartile
FROM {{ datasource_schema }}.dim_customer c
LEFT JOIN {{ datasource_schema }}.fact_order_header oh ON c.customer_id = oh.customer_id
LEFT JOIN {{ datasource_schema }}.fact_order_line ol ON oh.order_id = ol.order_id
GROUP BY 1
